value_source: NCVER, Terms and definitions: National VET Provider and VET in Schools Collections (revised September 2024)
rationale: Study mode is not an AVETMISS data element; it is an NCVER derived reporting concept defined in NCVER's own terms-and-definitions support document as full-time versus part-time, with scope column 'All' (covers GF, TVA, VETiS and VQCR), and the same document defines 'Full-time' and 'Part-time' as its two categories. Fetched through the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/<source url>) because ncver.edu.au serves a Cloudflare challenge to automated requests. The two categories are published; the numeric codes behind the _ID suffix are not, so values are given as labels. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review looked only at the AVETMISS data element definitions, which contain no study mode element (they have 'Delivery mode identifier', which TVA carries separately as DELIVERY_MODE_ID). Study mode is defined in NCVER's publication-level terms and definitions instead.

value_source: NCVER, Government-funded students and courses: explanatory notes (support document)
rationale: NCVER's terms-and-definitions document defines 'Provider reporting type' as a Government-funded (GF) collection concept and points to the Government-funded students and courses explanatory notes for its derivation; those notes describe it as a derived field built from submitter identifier and training organisation type identifier, and tabulate its five reporting categories. Fetched through the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/<source url>) because ncver.edu.au blocks automated requests. Category labels are published; the numeric codes behind the _ID suffix are not. Note the separate Government funding of VET (financial) collection uses a different eight-way provider-type split from 2019, which is not the classification for these fields. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier review searched the AVETMISS data element definitions, which do not contain provider reporting type. It is an NCVER derivation documented in the Government-funded students and courses explanatory notes, not in AVETMISS.

value_source: NCVER, Terms and definitions: National VET Provider and VET in Schools Collections (context only)
rationale: The PLIDA description itself names the two states ('registered active or not-registered in a collection year'), and NCVER's terms document supports the underlying distinction, defining registered training organisations as those listed on the National Training Register and noting training providers 'can be registered or non-registered'. No NCVER or AVETMISS codeframe publishes the numeric codes, so this is the shape only.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination was right that AVETMISS has no such element, but the description alone supports a two-state domain, which is now an allowed 'guessed' outcome.

value_domain: Short uppercase mnemonic for one of the eight published DEX 'Assessed by' categories (inferred; only SDJOINT is public)
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (1 March 2026), section 8.1 and section 12 list of data values
rationale: The DEX Protocols publish the eight 'Assessed by' categories, and the package already sources those labels for the label twin ASSESSEDBY in the same table. This column holds the CODE, not the label: the bulk upload specification shows <AssessedByCode>SDJOINT</AssessedByCode>, so the codes are short mnemonics. Only SDJOINT is public; the rest sit in the login-gated reference-data XML. Putting the eight label strings here would write label text into a code column.

The PLIDA description supplies two real values (FOFMS, EXTNL) and the field is a short uppercase mnemonic identifying the DSS system that supplied the activity record. I searched the DEX Protocols v13, the Bulk File Upload Technical Specification (Nov 2025) and the Web Services Technical Specification v1.11 and none of them contains a source-system code list; it is an internal DSS warehouse field, so the two documented values are the whole defensible domain.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier reviewer noted the two examples are not a complete codeframe, which is true, but two real published values are enough for a coarse inferred domain.

rationale: The field sits in the DEX calendar dimension table special_ref_calendar alongside THEDAY, THEDAYNAME, THEDAYOFYEAR, THEWEEK, THEISOWEEK, THEMONTH and THEMONTHNAME; with a separate THEDAYNAME holding the weekday label, THEDAYOFWEEK is the numeric weekday index taking 1 to 7. The numbering convention (Sunday-first as in SQL Server DATEPART, versus Monday-first as in ISO 8601) is not published, so only the range is claimed.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination treated the vague description ('Calendar related data fields') as fatal, but the variable name and its sibling columns fix the domain to a 1-7 weekday index.

rationale: Sibling columns in special_outlet are described as 'tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)', so the status of an outlet address is most plausibly the outcome of that validation step, taking a handful of short codes. No DEX Protocol, bulk upload spec or web services spec publishes the list, and a second reading (record status: current versus superseded) cannot be ruled out, so this is a coarse shape only and the specific labels are illustrative rather than sourced.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination was correct that no public codeframe exists; a coarse three-state status shape is now an allowed outcome, but treat it as low confidence.

rationale: The name parses as client address source validity code and the description calls it an address quality code, so it grades how well the supplied client address resolved through the DSS IQ Office Address Validation and Geocoder service that the sibling geography columns name. DSS publishes no code list for it in the Protocols, bulk upload spec or web services spec, so only the coarse ordered shape (a small number of match-quality grades) is defensible; the labels given are illustrative.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination was correct that no public codeframe exists; a coarse quality-grade shape is now allowed, at low confidence.

value_domain: DEX program, program activity or service type name (open text)
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (1 March 2026)
rationale: NAME is a free-text label, not a code: it occurs in three DEX reference tables (special_program, special_activity, special_service_type) and carries the name of the program, the program activity or the service type respectively. The sample values are real DEX names read off the fetched Protocols (the first five are DEX program names, the last is a service type named in section 6.2.2 guidance). The complete lists live in the DEX program specific guidance and service type matrix on dex.dss.gov.au, which returns 403 to automated requests, so the domain is an open text name domain rather than an enumerated codeframe.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination treated it as an unpublished codeframe. It is a name field, so an open text domain seeded with published DEX names is more faithful than typed missing.

values: students at risk of moving to long-term unemployment or unemployed former students
value_source: DSS, Try, Test and Learn (department program page, last modified 30 May 2025)
rationale: DSS names the Try, Test and Learn Fund priority groups on its own program page: three for tranche one (young parents; younger carers; students at risk of moving to long-term unemployment or unemployed former students) and two for tranche two (older unemployed people; at-risk young people). Confidence is medium because the same page records that applications were also accepted for other vulnerable groups at risk of long-term welfare dependence, so a residual 'other' category may exist in DEX, and DSS does not publish DEX's internal coding of these groups. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier reviewer called this a local list with no public codeframe. The fund is a published DSS program and DSS names its priority groups directly.

value_domain: four-character visa stream code, 0000 when unavailable (inferred)
rationale: Only the format and the fallback are supportable. The PLIDA description fixes the field at four characters with '0000' where no valid stream is present, and that is the single value whose meaning is published. The package's bundled codeframe inst/extdata/codeframes/visa_subclass.tsv carries a 'stream' column, but it is empty for all 82 subclass rows, so it supplies nothing. I found no Home Affairs numeric stream codeframe: streams are published only as named categories in statistical outputs (programme-level Skill, Family and Special Eligibility streams; subclass-level streams such as Short-term, Medium-term and Labour Agreement), never with the four-character codes used in the movements data. Attempts to reach a Home Affairs code list through immi.homeaffairs.gov.au and the Home Affairs visa statistics pages returned 404 or 403.
supersedes_rationale: The earlier determination stands on substance; the only change is that the documented four-character shape with '0000' as the published fallback can carry a low-confidence inferred domain instead of typed missing.
